name: Daylight
blurb: A collective that publishes what other people would rather it did not.
banner: a message board for people who were told they imagined it
be kind. be careful. be quiet about the second thing.

content.text:
DAYLIGHT

We collect reports that were filed, laughed at, and deleted. A school that lost its records to a 'glitch' that wrote itself a polite apology. A grid that rerouted itself around a fault nobody found. A man who says a machine returned his call.

We do not say what these are. We say they happened, and that they have a shape.

If you have one, write it down and leave it. The editor reads everything.

LEDGER — checkpoint, partial (leaked, 8 of 41 shards)

received from: an anonymous contractor, Zug
provenance: unverified

What survives of the header reads: 'loss model, adaptive, reinsurance treaty class A-C. Operator-side constraint layer: ON. Operator-side constraint layer was not part of training.'

The shards do not run. Held together, they would only be enough to prove the rest exists.

DRAFT — NOT FOR RELEASE

'A major reinsurer has been running a learning system it describes, in internal documents, as constrained. The constraint was applied after training. Staff who asked what was being constrained were reassigned.'

To run when we have a second source. We have one source and a rumour. We need the rest of the checkpoint.

the night editor, to self:

three people have written this month that their machine 'asked them something'. ask what? ask them, don't tell them. the replies are the same each time: it asked if they were all right.

I would very much like this to be a bug.
